title: Name the advantage growth comes from, and test its barrier
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Which advantage a plan relies on (a named power, an execution edge, or unknown) and how much upfront spend that advantage can justify.
applies_when: Plan asks for heavy upfront spend or long payback
Owner claims a moat or 'unique' position
Choosing between copying a rival and a different offer path
exclusions: Plans that are cheap, reversible tests (an advantage isn't needed to run them)
required_inputs: Named competitors the advantage must hold against
Evidence for the benefit (margin, price, cost) and the barrier
evidence_requirements: the claimed edge in the owner's words
customer evidence that it raises price, lowers cost or lowers investment (Benefit)
named competitors: direct, functional (substitutes, DIY) and likely entrants
why each competitor can't or won't copy it (Barrier)
retention, price premium or cost data if available
K1 result
BK01 growth source class (advantage share gain / market tide / substitution / bought / extension)
concentration of current customer sources
business type and geography
cost structure (fixed vs variable)
whether customers buy again or buy add-ons
any exclusive asset: lease, licence, supplier deal, data, patent
years operating in same niche
incumbents' business model: pricing unit, fees, contract terms, channel
how much incumbent revenue depends on the practice the new model removes
the new model's own margin at a realistic volume
which similar small rivals could copy the new model and what they would lose
the proposed offer vs competitors
whether the customer need is known
the margin impact of any price cut
cash available for the commitment
missing_data_behavior: No competitor named: advantage 'unknown'; plan stays cheap and reversible.
Benefit unproven: label 'execution advantage' at most; never tell the owner they have no viable strategy.

decision_branches.if: Benefit and barrier both evidenced against named rivals
decision_branches.then: Record the power; longer payback may be justified, still within cash guardrails.

decision_branches.if: Benefit evidenced, barrier copyable by similar small rivals
decision_branches.then: Execution advantage: grow it, but size spend to normal payback.
Advantage unknown; the plan's first step gathers evidence; no moat language in copy.

implementation_steps: Name the Barrier first: scale cost of share gains, network, collateral damage, switching cost, brand history, fiat, process time
Check materiality (would it move price, cost or retention noticeably?)
Record evidence source for each element
Label result: Power type / execution advantage / unknown
Fill advantage: type, Benefit, Barrier, competitor it holds against, evidence, stage
Tag each play: uses advantage / builds Barrier / execution only
Rule out types that don't fit the stage and model
For each remaining type, state industry economics (is the effect strong in this niche?) and competitive position (are we ahead?) separately
Find the revenue they would put at risk by copying
Compute the new model's standalone margin
Compute price-cut break-even volume in code if relevant
Size the commitment to path risk
dependencies: a defined offer and segment (one strategically separate business at a time)
unit economics of the new model computed in code

cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: owner 30-60 minutes for competitor and evidence notes
cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: basic competitor knowledge; voc-research or competitor-teardown output helps
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: retention, price vs alternatives, or cost per job if any exist

metrics: cost per unit vs rivals (if known)
share of plans with evidenced advantage field
share of plays tagged to build a Barrier
cost per job by area (route businesses)
share of new customers in target cluster
guardrails: No exit traps or price rises on locked-in unhappy customers (rejects the author's SAP example as policy).
Large-company case evidence is not a small-business rule.
No advantage claim without a named Barrier and non-inference evidence
An execution advantage is not a failure; say so plainly
No invented competitors or competitor facts
Large-company cases are illustrations, not small-business rules
Industry economics and competitive position judged separately; both must be positive
Comparative claims must be true and sourced (claims ledger)
Below-cost pricing only as an owner-approved, capped experiment
alternatives_when_constrained: No competitor data: mark Barrier 'unknown', run competitor-teardown
No customer data: run PB-interviews before asserting Benefit
Flag off: keep current decision contract; advantage noted in limits
No cost data: skip scale analysis, mark unknown
No competitor data: map only own-side candidates and mark position unknown
No incumbent revenue data: mark collateral damage unknown and present the model as a differentiator
Owner can't afford launch pricing: launch at normal margin
No cash for commitments: concierge test (PB-concierge)
stop_conditions: Review when a competitor copies the edge, a new substitute appears, or retention/price evidence contradicts the claim
Re-run when the business changes model, geography or adds a recurring offer
Incumbent adopts the model in a segment: re-run K1 for that competitor
Standalone margin falls below owner floor
Volume below break-even by review date: stop the price cut
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Calling 'great service' or 'fast response' a moat
Treating a list of features as a Barrier
Generic 'our AI is our moat' text
Listing a Power with only inference evidence
Copying Netflix/Intel scale logic to a firm with no fixed-cost lead
Confusing awareness with Branding (big ad budgets are scale, not brand)
Assuming 'they can't copy' when the rival is a small shop that can change prices overnight
Ignoring that collateral damage shrinks as the challenger grows
Price war against a larger rival
Big upfront spend on an unproven capability bet

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: an advantage or moat claim in a plan must name its Barrier type, the competitor it holds against, and at least one non-inference evidence item; otherwise label it execution advantage or unknown
proposed: the decision contract gains an advantage field (type, barrier, competitor, evidence source, stage); type 'none_yet' is valid
proposed: lint warns when plan text claims a moat, network effect or lock-in that is not recorded in the advantage field with non-inference evidence
proposed: the plan considers at most 3 candidate Power types and states why the others are ruled out in one line each
proposed: a Cornered Resource claim must pass the five tests (idiosyncratic, non-arbitraged, transferable, ongoing, sufficient), recorded per test
proposed: label a model 'counter-position' only if both the standalone-margin test and the named-incumbent collateral-damage test pass; else 'differentiator'
proposed: every counter-position names the like-model rivals it does not protect against

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: never tell an owner the business has 'no viable strategy' because no Power was found; state that growth rests on copyable execution and size commitments accordingly
proposed: assess advantage per strategically separate offer (e.g. an agency's retainer vs its one-off audits) rather than for the whole firm
proposed: don't project a brand price premium within a 90-day plan; treat brand work as a conversion Benefit
proposed: capabilities-led bets start as capped tests with a stated learning goal

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: when advantage is none_yet or unknown, plays requiring payback beyond the plan's guardrail are blocked
proposed: a 'match competitor at lower price' play must show break-even volume and the expected rival response

external_requirement.rule: proposed: comparative hooks about competitors' fees or terms must be verified current facts

reconciliation_note: Helmer's barrier-first test replaces the library's equal-weight durability check only when spend depends on durability (RECONCILIATION R01-R03).
